Estimate the memory parameter

estimate_memory.Rd

Estimates the memory parameter \(d\) from the leading score process, the centred curves projected onto the leading eigenfunction of a covariance-type operator. If the estimate is near the upper end of its search interval, the score process is integer differenced and \(d\) is estimated again, until the estimate falls below the upper end. The number of differences is then added back to the estimate.

Usage

estimate_memory(
  x,
  method = c("bc_lpwn2", "bc_lpwn1", "lpwn2", "lpwn1", "lw", "dfa"),
  cov_type = c("sample", "lrc_RS", "lrc_LRS"),
  m_const = 0.75,
  B = 100,
  burn_in = 200,
  R_noise = 0,
  tuning_const = 1,
  cov_band_const = 1,
  dfa_levels = 50,
  dfa_minnpts = 3,
  dfa_cutoff = 10^c(0.7, 2.5),
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A matrix of curves (grid points by time).

method

Estimator: "lw" (local Whittle), "dfa" (detrended fluctuation analysis), "lpwn1" or "lpwn2" (local polynomial Whittle with noise, with one or two polynomial correction terms), or "bc_lpwn1" or "bc_lpwn2" (BC-LPWN1 or BC-LPWN2, the LPWN estimate bias-corrected by the prefiltered sieve bootstrap).

cov_type

Operator of the FPCA that gives the leading eigenfunction: "sample" (empirical covariance operator), "lrc_RS" (long-run covariance operator with an adaptive bandwidth) or "lrc_LRS" (long-run covariance operator in sandwich form).

m_const

Bandwidth exponent \(a\), so that \(\lfloor 1 + T^a \rfloor\) frequencies are used.

B, burn_in

Number of bootstrap samples and burn-in length (BC-LPWN).

R_noise

Number of polynomial terms for the noise in LPWN.

tuning_const

Constant \(c\). The score process is differenced while the estimate is at least \(1 - c / \log m\).

cov_band_const

Bandwidth constant for cov_type = "lrc_LRS".

dfa_levels, dfa_minnpts, dfa_cutoff

Number of block sizes, minimum number of points per block and range of block sizes in the DFA regression.

seed

Optional seed for the bootstrap.

verbose

Whether to show progress.

Value

An object of class farfima_memory with the estimate d and the leading score process scores. BC-LPWN also returns the uncorrected estimate d_initial, the bias and the bootstrap estimates.

Details

The local Whittle and LPWN code is adapted from the LongMemoryTS package (Leschinski, Voges and Wenger, 2019), and the DFA code from the fArma package (Wuertz, Setz and Chalabi, 2017).

See also

frac_diff() to difference the curves with the estimate, and farfima() for the whole fit.

Examples

x = sim_farfima(n = 300, d = 0.3, p = 1, q = 0, seed = 1)
estimate_memory(x, method = "lw")
#> Memory estimate d = 0.6358
#>   LW on the leading score process of the empirical covariance operator (Covar), bandwidth exponent 0.75
estimate_memory(x, method = "lpwn2")
#> Memory estimate d = 0.5871
#>   LPWN2 on the leading score process of the empirical covariance operator (Covar), bandwidth exponent 0.75
